• Common name: Largescale rasbora
  • Origin: Thailand
  • Available size: 2-3 cm

In coloration Rasbora paucisqualis is intermediate between the typical rasboras with a dark longitudinal stripe and the harlequin rasboras (Trigonostigma). This charming species attains a maximum length of 3-4 cm. It is a nice addition to the available dwarf fish species from southeastern Asia.

Nothing is known so far about the spawning behaviour of the species. It would be very interesting to know whether it spawns in a normal "Rasbora-like" manner or upside-down like the Trigonostigma species.

The fish first arrived as a shipment of very small (about 1 cm) rasboras from Thailand and were provisionally named "Rasbora sp. Dwarf" before being identified as Rasbora paucisqualis.

Lexicon: Rasbora: after a common name of one of the species used in Bengal. paucisqualis: means "with few scales". Trigonostigma: ancient Greek, means "with a triangular spot".
